VERDICT: LGTM

The new `AssignOwnerCapacityWarning` is a precise structural mirror of the existing `AssignOwnerBulkSignupWarning`: a single small function class, one public `service` method, `@Val Owner` mutate-in-place, wired as its own pipeline step under `govern: [ transaction ]` between the existing warning steps. Naming (`AssignOwner<Warning>`), placement in `.../function/owner/`, and the "runs before SaveOwner so the count reflects existing owners only" reasoning all match the established convention.

The Owner model getter/setter/column, the schema additions across all four DB dialects, and the OpenAPI `readOnly` field follow the exact form of the sibling `bulkSignupWarning` / `possibleDuplicate` fields.

On the one plausible concern — the city-count-case-insensitive stream is also present in `RequireCityCapacity` — this is not a structural defect in this codebase. Each of these small functions is deliberately self-contained and does its own `findAll().stream()` count (bulk-signup counts by date, capacity-require counts by city); the two classes have distinct responsibilities (hard reject-and-throw vs. compute-and-set a warning flag) and run as separate pipeline steps. Extracting a shared helper would cut against the "one small function class per step" idiom the project is built on, not reinforce it. Keeping warn and reject as separate steps is the natural choice here. The Javadoc even cross-references `RequireCityCapacity` for the shared case-insensitivity rule, which is the right way to keep them coherent without coupling them.
